name: The Osage Oranges of the Torre Girona Gardens

location.address: Jardins de Torre Girona, Carrer de Jordi Girona 31, Barcelona (UPC Campus Nord)

access: Free, public urban park (transferred from UPC university management to Barcelona City Council management under an April 2019 agreement, same as bcn_026/027/028 in the same garden); posted seasonal opening hours, gated at night.
transport: Palau Reial (Metro L3), about 10 min walk
verify_notes: Register: Ajuntament de Barcelona AIL catalogue, CC BY 4.0, register_id 99400680106, catalogue no. 0194-04-19, catalogued 2021, girth 1.9m, height 8m, crown 6m, units=14, no planting year recorded (register field blank, 'Per determinar'). Collectibility: this is an old double row (doble alineacio) of osage oranges, thoroughly mixed into the garden's forest vegetation, catalogued by the ajuntament as ONE item (one catalogue number) rather than 14 separate designations; the ajuntament's own description calls the species barely used today with very few examples in Barcelona, which is what makes the row worth seeing rather than an ordinary planting. It is a compact curiosity within the same small garden as bcn_026/027/028 (the two stone pines, the Aleppo pine and the bottle tree, all already published from this same garden), not a boulevard: treating it as one collectible stop on the same short walk. Same source (diarieljardi.cat, an independent Catalan gardens journal) that bcn_026 already cites also describes this same garden in detail. Age: no planting year or age given by the register or either source; leaving age_estimate empty per the missing-age rule rather than guessing, flagging so a future pass or reader can supply a girth-based estimate or the reader can be asked. Alive and public: same access situation as the three already-published Torre Girona trees, transferred from UPC to city park management in April 2019, no closure or removal reports found. Species check: Maclura pomifera is the Osage Orange, native to the south-central US (Arkansas/Louisiana region, hence the Catalan nickname 'tarongers de Louisiana', Louisiana oranges); the canonical English common name for the species page is Osage Orange, not the literal translation of the local nickname.
